summary.headline: Alldigi Q2 FY27 revenue rose 4% YoY to INR153.3 crore, while EBITDA grew about 29% to INR46.3 crore at a 30.2% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR153.3 crore (+4% YoY, +2% QoQ), with H1 revenue at INR303.6 crore (+4.2%). Profitability grew much faster than revenue: Q2 EBITDA rose about 29% YoY to INR46.3 crore and PAT rose about 51% YoY to INR26.6 crore. Growth was held back by a deliberate reduction in low-margin domestic BPM, which fell 33% YoY in Q2, while international revenue rose 15.1% and now makes up about 70% of revenue. Management also announced a buyback of up to 4.8 lakh shares at INR1,000 per share (about INR48 crore), and new-business ACV for H1 more than doubled to INR82.6 crore.

segments.name: BPM
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR111.6 crore (+1% YoY, +1.8% QoQ); H1 INR221.3 crore (+1.4%). International BPM grew 12.6% YoY in Q2 and is about 83% of BPM revenue (75% a year ago), while domestic BPM fell 33% YoY.

segments.name: BPM segment margin
segments.commentary: Q2 segment profit INR17.5 crore at 15.6% (11.6% a year ago, 11.9% in Q1); H1 INR30.6 crore at about 13.8%.

segments.name: Tech & Digital (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR41.7 crore (+12.9% YoY, +2.7% QoQ); H1 INR82.3 crore (+12.4%). Employee records processed were 51.1 lakh in Q2 (+7.2% YoY) and 101.3 lakh in H1.

segments.name: T&D segment margin
segments.commentary: Q2 segment profit INR18.3 crore at 43.9%; H1 INR35.7 crore at about 43.4%, helped by higher volumes and international mix.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the employee cost-to-revenue ratio to keep falling, with headcount reduction continuing; full effect of Q2 headcount reduction (started mid-Q2) expected in Q3.
BPM margin is expected to keep improving as domestic BPM is run down, but management gave no quantum; the domestic exit continues only where clients remain profitable.
Management declined to give revenue guidance for the next few quarters. BPM deals are expected to ramp in about 3-4 months; T&D ramp takes longer, possibly 2-4 quarters.
T&D guided to early double-digit growth over the next three years.
Lease payments expected to stay in the same range as FY26 (about INR35 crore base), potentially lower with resource optimisation.
Buyback of up to 4.8 lakh equity shares at INR1,000 per share (about INR48 crore), subject to approvals. Dividend policy is cited as consistent with the buyback.
capex_capacity: New BOT (build-operate-transfer) captive service started with one client: over 1,000 FTEs now, with the client targeting 2-3x growth; a separate BOT deal is valued at about INR16.8 crore on a contract of about 2 quarters, with potential to reach 3,000-4,000 FTEs.
Manila operations were significantly optimised; management called Manila a high-cost location.
Office was replaced with a new one on a longer lease commitment, raising ROU assets from roughly INR50-60 crore to about INR140-150 crore.

Products launched: Buzzily 2.0 (May 2026); Alldigi 360 (HCM suite incl. payroll, SaaS or technology-only) and Alldigi 360 Analytics (AI analytics, standalone or on top of existing HRIS) in October 2026.
demand_pricing: Q2 new business ACV INR37.2 crore: one Europe T&D deal of about INR7 crore (multi-year, auto-renewing, about 60%+ gross margin) and one BPM BOT deal of about INR16.8 crore.

Payroll pricing is under pressure: management said clients expect gain-share on efficiencies, so per-transaction prices tend to fall over time, while growth is sought through cross-selling HCM, SaaS and analytics.
Workday Silver certification held; design batch to finish mid-November 2026. Management sees about 4 clients in the pipeline for Workday connector implementations.
TaxSpanner partnership live since last year; management expects a bigger push this year, with more than 10-12 lakh employee records in India as the addressable base, but gave no revenue guidance.
Sales organisation rebuilt: new CBO for BPM, BPM-background leaders for US sales, SMB and enterprise sales teams in T&D, and a Southeast Asia BPM sales effort that has produced early Q2 ACV wins.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall about INR5 crore (about 7%) QoQ while headcount fell less?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower replacement costs from tighter hiring rates, Manila optimisation (a high-cost location), and a retiral-benefit true-up. The full headcount reduction, which began mid-Q2, will show in Q3, and the employee cost-to-revenue ratio should keep falling.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic BPM rationalisation complete?
qa_highlights.answer: It is ongoing. Management decided to exit some large client relationships and will not add new domestic clients, but will keep profitable existing ones, so the domestic book shrinks continuously rather than being fully exited.

qa_highlights.question: How far can payroll price erosion go, and how much revenue per employee can be extracted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price points fall as efficiencies are shared with clients through gain-share, but premium services hold price. The focus is on selling additional HCM, SaaS and analytics services rather than defending transaction prices.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue and timing prospects for the new ACV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide quarterly revenue. BPM ramp-up is about 3-4 months from go-live, while T&D takes longer, possibly 2-4 quarters, depending on client implementation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise from about INR69 crore to about INR80 crore while DSO fell from 77 to 74 days?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said receivables are billed plus unbilled, and the rise reflects unbilled balances being converted into bills after project milestones, along with business acceleration. DSO is expected to fall further.

qa_highlights.question: How does the segment profit total of INR35.8 crore reconcile with reported EBITDA of about INR46 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said segment profit is measured before finance costs, depreciation and unallocated costs, so it is not comparable with EBITDA and no clean bridge was given.

risks_watch: Revenue growth remains low at about 4%, with domestic BPM still declining, so the margin story depends on international ramp-ups converting to revenue.
Q2 receivables rose and standalone receivables were up about 46% in six months; management attributes this to timing, so DSO and unbilled balances need tracking.
Payroll price erosion through gain-share, which is structural per management's own answer.
Cash fell to INR127.2 crore after the dividend; the buyback (about INR48 crore) will reduce it further.
Execution risk on BOT and large deal ramp-ups (1,000 FTEs now, targeted 3,000-4,000) and on T&D implementation timelines.
Workday certification and NPS integration are at an early stage with no revenue quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, margins and the sales pipeline, but guarded on revenue timing and the drivers of the headline growth rate. Management declined to give quarterly revenue guidance and gave no quantum for BPM margin uplift; NPS and Workday revenue are described as too early to quantify. The receivables answers were defensive and attributed the increase to timing and unbilled-to-billed conversion.
key_quotes: While revenue growth remains moderate, our profitability continues to grow significantly faster than revenue, reflecting operating leverage and improved business mix and disciplined cost management.
Our focus remains on profitable and sustainable growth rather than pursuing revenue at the expense of margins.
So it's a matter of whether it is another 2 or 3 quarters or 4 quarters.
